description: A project-based graduate laboratory in which teams specify, build, integrate, test and demonstrate a mobile robot that completes a navigation challenge. Students work on the hardware bench and in the code runner, plan the project with schedules and risk registers, and pass a safety review before the final demonstration.
modelledOn: Siegwart, Nourbakhsh and Scaramuzza, Introduction to Autonomous Mobile Robots
outcomes: Derive requirements and a functional architecture for a mobile robot and verify them with a test plan.
Integrate sensors, motor drivers, a microcontroller and a single-board computer into a working robot with documented interfaces.
Implement odometry, reactive control, obstacle avoidance and grid path planning, and tune them from logged data.
Debug hardware and software faults systematically using logs, recordings and fault injection.
Plan a team project with a work breakdown, critical path, risk register and budget.
Conduct a safety review and present a demonstration and technical report that honestly reports results and failures.

units.title: Systems engineering for robots
topics: Stakeholder needs, use cases and measurable requirements
Functional decomposition, block diagrams and interface control documents
Trade studies and budgets for power, mass, compute and cost in cedis
The V-model: verification and validation planning
Robot architecture patterns: sense-plan-act, layered and behaviour-based
Team tooling: version control, issue tracking and automated checks

units.title: Hardware and software integration
topics: Sensor and actuator interfaces: I2C, SPI, UART, PWM and ADC
Motor drivers, encoders, power distribution and brown-out behaviour
Microcontroller firmware: timer interrupts and fixed-rate control loops
Single-board computer integration and publish-subscribe messaging with MQTT
Sensor calibration and filtering: moving average, complementary and Kalman filters
Integration testing: bench tests, hardware-in-the-loop and stub drivers

units.title: Mobile robot navigation challenge
topics: Differential-drive kinematics and wheel odometry
Reactive behaviours: line and wall following, PID tuning
Obstacle sensing with ultrasonic, infrared and lidar sensors
Occupancy grids and localisation with a particle filter
Grid path planning with Dijkstra and A*
Challenge rules, scoring and run strategy

units.title: Debugging and logging
topics: Systematic debugging: reproduce, hypothesise, bisect and verify
Logging levels, timestamps and structured telemetry
Data recording, replay and plotting
Fault injection, failure modes and watchdogs
Root-cause analysis and blameless post-mortems

units.title: Team project planning
topics: Scope, work breakdown structure and milestones
Gantt charts and critical path analysis
Roles, sprints and stand-ups in a hardware project
Risk register: spares, supply chain delays and mitigation in Ghana
Bill of materials and budget control

units.title: Safety review
topics: Hazard identification and FMEA for a mobile robot
Emergency stop, interlocks and fail-safe design
Electrical safety and lithium battery handling
Software safety: limits, watchdogs and safe states
Safety review board: scenario-based review and sign-off

units.title: Build, test and iterate
topics: Integration sprints and subsystem acceptance tests
Regression testing after every change
Field trials: lighting, floor surface, battery level and interference
Performance measurement: success rate, time and repeatability
Design reviews and the iteration decision

units.title: Demonstration and report
topics: Demonstration script, rehearsal and contingency plan
Technical report structure and figures
Reporting results and failures honestly
Peer review, lessons learned and handover documentation

schedule.title: Requirements, decomposition and budgets
schedule.exercise: Write ten measurable requirements for a robot that must navigate a corridor course and stop at a target, draw its block diagram with interfaces, and make a power and cost budget for the chosen parts.

tasks.title: Turn a stakeholder brief for a corridor delivery robot into ten measurable requirements, each with a test method and pass threshold
Draw a functional block diagram of a navigation robot with labelled signals between sensors, controller and motors, and list each interface
Build a power budget for motors, sensors and a single-board computer, size the battery for a 45 minute run and check it against the cost limit

schedule.title: Verification planning, architecture and tooling
schedule.exercise: Make a verification matrix linking each requirement to a test, choose an architecture for the challenge and justify it, and set up a repository with a branching rule and issue labels.

tasks.title: Create a repository, commit a firmware skeleton on a feature branch, merge it with a review comment and tag the first release
Draw a V-model for the robot, linking each requirement to the verification test that closes it and to the test level
Compare sense-plan-act and behaviour-based architectures for a cluttered corridor in a branching case, choose one and defend the trade-offs

schedule.title: Sensor, motor and firmware interfaces
schedule.exercise: Wire an ultrasonic sensor, a motor driver and an encoder to a microcontroller, write a fixed-rate control loop with a timer interrupt, and verify the loop period with measurement.

tasks.title: Read a distance from an ultrasonic sensor on a microcontroller, print it every 100 ms and check it against a ruler at five distances
Drive two motors with PWM through a motor driver, read encoder ticks and plot speed against duty cycle over ten settings
Write firmware with a timer interrupt that runs a 50 Hz control loop, and measure jitter to confirm the period stays within 5 percent

schedule.title: Messaging, calibration and integration testing
schedule.exercise: Publish sensor readings from a microcontroller to a single-board computer over MQTT, calibrate and filter a noisy sensor, and write a bench test that uses stub drivers.

tasks.title: Publish distance readings to an MQTT topic from the robot and subscribe to them on the computer, checking message rate and loss
Calibrate an infrared sensor with a lookup of 10 measured distances and compare a moving average with a complementary filter on noisy data
Write a stub-driver test harness that replays recorded sensor data into the navigation code and asserts the expected motor commands

schedule.title: Kinematics, odometry and reactive control
schedule.exercise: Derive the pose update equations for a differential-drive robot, estimate drift over a 4 m square path, and tune a PID wall follower.

tasks.title: Compute the pose of a differential-drive robot from encoder ticks along a 2 m square and plot the path with the final position error
Implement a proportional line follower with three reflectance sensors and report the mean lateral error for three gain values
Tune a PID wall-following controller in a simulation, compare rise time, overshoot and steady-state error, and explain the final gains

schedule.title: Obstacle sensing, mapping and localisation
schedule.exercise: Compare ultrasonic, infrared and lidar readings of the same obstacles, build an occupancy grid from a scan log and localise the robot with a particle filter in a known map.

tasks.title: Measure the same five obstacles with ultrasonic and infrared sensors, tabulate errors and note which surfaces cause bad readings
Build an occupancy grid from a log of range scans and poses, and display cells as free, occupied or unknown
Implement a particle filter with 500 particles to localise a robot in a known corridor map and report the position error over 100 steps

schedule.title: Path planning and challenge strategy
schedule.exercise: Plan routes through the challenge map with Dijkstra and A*, compare node counts, and write a run strategy that balances speed against the penalty for touching obstacles.

tasks.title: Run A* and Dijkstra on a 20x20 grid map with obstacles and compare nodes expanded and path length for three goals
Implement A* on the challenge map with inflated obstacles, convert the path to waypoints and drive them in simulation
Choose a run strategy for the challenge in a scoring case, trading speed for obstacle penalties, and compare expected score across three plans

schedule.title: Debugging, logging and post-mortems
schedule.exercise: Add structured logging to the robot code, replay a failed run, find the root cause of a drifting turn with a hypothesis log, and write a blameless post-mortem.

tasks.title: Add timestamped logs at three levels to a navigation program and record a run with sensor, command and state values every 100 ms
Replay a recorded run, plot commanded against measured wheel speed, and locate the moment the robot first diverges from the plan
Inject a stuck sensor and a battery sag into the robot, verify the watchdog drives it to a safe stop, and record the response time

schedule.title: Project plans, risks and budgets
schedule.exercise: Produce a work breakdown, Gantt chart and critical path for the term project, a risk register with at least eight risks including late parts, and a bill of materials within budget.

tasks.title: Draw a work breakdown structure for the robot project with at least 25 tasks, an owner for each and four milestones
Build a Gantt chart with dependencies, compute the critical path and show how a two-week delay in parts delivery moves the end date
Respond to a supply chain delay for motor drivers in a branching case, weighing local substitutes, scope cuts and schedule slip against the budget

schedule.title: Hazards, safe states and safety review
schedule.exercise: Run an FMEA for the robot, design an emergency stop and a battery handling procedure, and defend the safety case in front of a mock review board.

tasks.title: List eight hazards of the robot with cause, effect, severity and a proposed control, in an FMEA table ranked by risk
Wire an emergency stop that cuts motor power independently of the microcontroller and test that it works while the firmware is hung
Present the safety case to a simulated review board, answer questions on battery and collision hazards, and fix the gaps listed in its findings

schedule.title: Integration sprints and acceptance tests
schedule.exercise: Run an integration sprint with acceptance tests per subsystem, add regression tests for each bug fixed, and plan field trials across floor surfaces and battery levels.

tasks.title: Run an acceptance test for the drive subsystem, driving straight for 3 m five times, and record the cross-track error against the threshold
Write regression tests that replay three recorded fault cases, run them after each code change and report any test that newly fails
Plan and run field trials on two floor surfaces at full and low battery, and report how drift and stopping distance change with each factor

schedule.title: Measuring performance and design reviews
schedule.exercise: Measure success rate, completion time and repeatability over twenty challenge runs, then hold a design review that decides which of three fixes to make before the demonstration.

tasks.title: Compute success rate, mean time and standard deviation over 20 logged challenge runs, and plot completion time per run
Compare two controller versions over 20 runs each with a confidence interval and decide whether the improvement is real
Decide which fixes to make before the demonstration in a design review case, weighing risk, remaining time and expected score gain

schedule.title: Demonstration, report and lessons learned
schedule.exercise: Rehearse and deliver the challenge demonstration, write the technical report with requirement results and failure analysis, and review another team's report.

tasks.title: Write a demonstration script with timing, roles and a contingency plan for three likely failures, and rehearse it in a scenario
Generate the report figures from run logs, covering the path, error over time and a results table, and caption each so it stands alone
Review a draft report that overstates its results, flag claims the data does not support and rewrite three passages to report failures honestly
